text.5_Tazria, 0_Chapter, 0_Paragraph: "A woman, when she shall seed and give birth to a male, etc. (Leviticus 12:2). And our Sages of blessed memory said (in Berakhot 60a and Niddah 31a): 'If the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male,' etc. And this is wondrous.The philosophers strained themselves to settle [this matter by arguing] that because the woman emits seed first, the 'drop' of the male comes last, and 'the upper one prevails.' This is not the case, however, if the man emits seed first, [as the female drop would then come last].However, in truth, this is a great strain on the explanation of the expression 'if the woman emits seed first,' which implies that specifically from her comes the seeding of the male, and not through the fact that the male seeds last.Furthermore, our Sages said at the end of the third chapter of Niddah regarding Dinah: it is written 'his daughter' (referring to Jacob), whereas regarding the [other] tribes it is written 'the sons of Leah'—because the woman emitted seed first. If so, it is understood that specifically from the seed of the woman the male is born (and this is enough for the wise). (And so it is in Midrash Rabbah on Tazria, end of chapter 14: 'the male is from the woman,' etc., see there).The explanation of the matter is that the 'Male' is the aspect of Chesed (Kindness), as it is written: 'He remembered (Zachar) His kindness (Chasdo)'; and the 'Female' is the aspect of Gevurah (Severity), [as in the phrase] 'The law of the kingdom is law' (Dina d’Malchuta Dina).And as our Sages said regarding our mother Sarah: at the moment the angels brought her the news that she was destined to give birth to a male son, she 'became a Niddah' (menstruated), which is the aspect of Gevurot (Severities). And our Sages also said that Abraham commanded to give [the guests] 'fine flour' (Solet), but she gave 'coarse flour' (Kemach); from here we learn that 'a woman's eye is narrow regarding guests'—and this is because she is from the aspect of Gevurot."
